RoomType.rationale: EntomancerElite.cs:9 => RoomType.Elite. "entomancer" is placed in `_hive_rooms().elite_keys` and nowhere else, matching the pool-classification convention (RoomType lives at pool-membership level in the sim). No `Tags` override in the C# (EntomancerElite does not declare `Tags`, so it inherits the empty default) and correspondingly "entomancer" is absent from `_hive_rooms().tags` -- consistent, no hook entry needed for the (non-overridden) Tags member.

AllPossibleMonsters.maps_to: no per-encounter counterpart; full_env.py::_monster_classes() (global Monster-subclass walk)
AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: EntomancerElite.cs:11 declares a single-element list containing only `Entomancer`, exactly GenerateMonsters' one and only draw. Same consumer census as the rest of the batch: the C# property's only two real readers (`ActModel.AllMonsters`->`ModelDb.Monsters`->`UnlockConsoleCmd.cs`'s dev-console unlock list and `NGeneralStatsGrid.cs:164`'s bestiary ratio) are UI/debug surfaces absent from this headless sim; `full_env.py::_monster_classes()`'s global class walk already includes `Entomancer` without needing a per-encounter declaration. Cost: none observed.

GenerateMonsters.rationale: EntomancerElite.cs:13-16: a single `Entomancer` instance, tuple slot `null`, zero RNG draws in GenerateMonsters itself (the only per-encounter Rng use anywhere in this fight family is the monster's own move-machine logic, not roster generation). `entomancer.py` does not override `create_monsters` at all -- `ENTOMANCER_ELITE = Encounter(id="entomancer_elite", monster_classes=[Entomancer])` relies on the base `Encounter.create_monsters` (`monsters/base.py`), which for a single fixed class with no `monster_slots` produces `[Entomancer(hooks, rng)]` with no slot assignment (the `zip(monsters, self.monster_slots)` loop is a no-op against the default empty `monster_slots=()`) and, correctly, zero draws off `selection_rng`. Roster (1x Entomancer), order, slot (null/unset) and draw count (0) all match. Re-executed the killing-blow context this unit is named for in the batch brief: `cmds.py`'s damage pipeline (`DamageCmd.deal`) already guards `if not was_lethal: hooks.on_damage_received(...)`, so the AfterDamageReceived-on-a-kill skip C#'s `CreatureCmd.cs:392`-style guard requires is honoured -- this is a `cmds`/killing-blow mechanism, not an `encounter` hook, and it is not GenerateMonsters' concern; noted here only because the brief named it as this unit's calibration context, and it is confirmed already fixed, not a live gap in this record's scope.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: `EncounterModel.cs:39` default (`=> false`), not overridden by the sealed `EntomancerElite`. The sim's `Encounter` object is never registered as a hook listener.

guards.what: Gold ladder (MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward) and ShouldGiveRewards -- both inherited, not overridden by EntomancerElite
guards.rationale: RoomType.Elite => 35-45 gold (EncounterModel.cs:64-81), matched by `rewards.py:170-173`'s `GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.ELITE] = (35, 45)` (non-ascension baseline). `ShouldGiveRewards` default `true` matched by `Encounter.should_give_rewards`'s dataclass default, unmodified by `ENTOMANCER_ELITE`.
